items.topic: Pressure level, local wall and nonlinear capacity
items.finding: The f5 source screens are 1.143285 and 1.083205. The peak-compression local-wall sensitivity is 1.033223 and 0.978132; the 019 sensitivity is below unity. Common-q 1.258252 rows exceed both declared screens.
items.remaining: A validated local bending/axial interaction, imperfection response and coupled nonlinear capacity are needed. Source 041's verified perfect nonlinear path belongs to its selected f4 section, not these re-sized f5 witnesses.

items.topic: Actual end moments and joint stresses
items.finding: The fold uses actual FE end moments and correlated axial/bending/torsional demands. It does not add the older dimensional joint proxy. Each design has 1500 end interfaces, with source joints sized to the target and no extra scalar reserve.
items.remaining: Joint rotational stiffness, local contact, SiC end damage, adhesive peel, shear-induced principal tension, hoop stress and residual stress still require resolved fields and qualification.

items.finding: Per-member peaks are applied over whole members; a second envelope applies the global maximum everywhere. Complete-member common-scale and coupon-volume calibrations are separate hypotheses and give very different probabilities.
items.remaining: Calibrate the actual stress-field and size transfer. A common complete-member scale despite unequal lengths must not be silently reinterpreted as a volume-calibrated material constant. Zero positive longitudinal stress does not close multiaxial tension risk.

items.finding: All headline probabilities are tube-fracture-only and omit joints, membrane, instability, shared batches and degradation. Equal allocation at frame Pf=1e-6 is approximately 1.333334e-9 per member.
items.remaining: Define whole-system risk allocation, valid component marginals, dependence/common-cause model and service duration/load spectrum with aging and crack-growth evidence.

items.finding: Illustrative 1.25-times-screen axial tests reach 1.00213 and 0.94965 MN and exceed the respective source screen. The frames require 750 part screens and qualification of 1500 end interfaces; amplified bending does not scale solely with axial-force ratio.
items.remaining: Validate proof fixtures, stress coverage, confinement and damage effects, inspection detection, accept/reject criteria and lifetime treatment. Supplier capability, throughput, scrap and pricing remain unknown.

items.finding: The frozen rise-8 force solution remains independently unverified. The new f5 closure data are a different geometry and loading case.
items.remaining: No rise-8 reliability claim can be closed by this fold. An independently admitted rise-8 solution and a defined transfer would be needed before using it as the new selected frame's demand.

items.claim: The dent-growth criterion is this seat's derivation: the face's fixed membrane force pR/4 on a paraboloid dent's curvature, against the core's crush strength less its share of the pressure, with the patch's plate buckling force taken off. No opened page prints it. Castanie, the CAI literature on face wrinkling over crushed core, and McGowan and Ambur's preload threshold support the mechanism, not the numbers.
items.needed_to_ground: Compression-after-impact tests on beryllium-faced CR-III coupons at 300 MPa, dented at 0.25-2 mm over 30-100 mm.

items.claim: The lost-core patch is read clamped (54.8 mm) and simply supported (27.1 mm); the real edge, a face continuous over intact core, lies between. The pressure that holds the face on the crushed core is a barrier this static reading ignores.
items.needed_to_ground: A plate-on-crushable-foundation analysis of the dented patch, or the coupon test above.

items.claim: The dent model (face membrane plus core crush over a plastic spread) is this seat's. It reads Pach's test within its 1.1-1.2 mm and 30 mm, and Clarke's FE at about half the FE depth. Hail is read three ways (fluid, Shi-calibrated, all energy) that span ten times in depth.
items.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a beryllium-faced CR-III panel at 25-75 mm and IEC velocities.

items.claim: No impact, puncture or through-thickness ductility data exist for thin SR-200 sheet. NASA 1971 calls beryllium's impact resistance extremely low. A cracked outer face vents its core cells; whether the CR-III core is perforated (034's evacuation of every cell) decides whether a crack vents the whole core.
items.needed_to_ground: Drop and ice-ball tests on 0.8 mm SR-200 sheet over honeycomb, and the core venting design.

items.claim: Each dent is scored alone against gamma 0.564; the as-built imperfection already spends that allowance, so a dent and the as-built shape compete for it.
items.needed_to_ground: 015's map with two interacting imperfections, or a measured shell.

items.claim: No hail flux (stones per square metre per storm, by size) was sourced, so the number of tube strikes in a storm is not given.
items.needed_to_ground: A hail climatology for the site.

items.claim: The tube's hail stress uses a shallow-shell-on-foundation reading of a cylinder, a static contact pressure (fluid or Shi-calibrated), no dynamic amplification, and the 14 mm Hexoloy tube data without size scaling. Birds, timber debris and tool drops on the tubes are not scored. No SiC tube impact test was found.
items.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a 275 mm, 1.14 mm-wall SiC tube.

items.claim: No Zylon/PBO film exists as a sourced product: no modulus, toughness, puncture or tear data. The tear lengths use other films' toughness and a projected modulus. The film is also unprotected from daylight (35 percent strength after six months).
items.needed_to_ground: A built 0/90 PBO film with barrier, tested for puncture, slit tear under biaxial load and UV.

items.claim: The lost-member screen is linear, rigid-jointed, on f4/f5 geodesics not at 022d's spacing, with lumped pressure loads; joint stiffness is unknown and no nonlinear collapse was run. 026b's discrete model is the place to repeat it.
items.needed_to_ground: A nonlinear frame analysis with one member removed, on 026b's model with the real joint stiffness.

items.claim: The film over the two bays a lost member leaves is scored at the same rise-to-span, a tension 1.5 times higher; the real film shape after loss is not modelled.
items.needed_to_ground: A membrane analysis of the rhombic bay.

items.claim: The descent model is a rigid sphere in ISA with an isothermal fill, a constant drag coefficient 0.2-0.47, added mass 0.5 rho V and no wind; the neutral-buoyancy pressure result assumes the inside air takes the outside temperature.
items.needed_to_ground: A coupled thermal and trajectory model, and the site's atmosphere.

items.claim: At a hole the face reads twice its membrane stress and yields out to 3.9 hole radii; whether the edge crumples and the hole grows while the slow leak keeps the load on is not modelled.
items.needed_to_ground: A hole-edge analysis of the sandwich at 300 MPa, or a punctured coupon under biaxial compression.

items.claim: No inspection limit was sourced for beryllium faces, SiC tubes or PBO film; the tap-test PoD is for 0.5 mm aluminium and falls with face thickness. Access to a 1257 m2 hull at 500 m is not addressed.

items.finding: The zero continuous-field mismatch shear and homogenized free-edge model create most of the new floats. retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: 037's shear-lag screen holds each face at the core's expansion (0.227 after the 250 F cure). That needs the core to carry 47 times the in-plane force at which its walls yield. CR-1457, Hexcel AGU 075b and NASA TM-4585 treat the core's in-plane stiffness and thermal force as negligible; on that premise the continuous core carries no mismatch shear and a free core edge reads 1.17 / 0.83.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A curved Be/CR-III panel cured with AF 163-2U, cycled over 271-302 K, strain-gauged at a core splice, at a face scarf and in the field, then sectioned.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: The free-edge shear uses this seat's homogenised model: K_biax from wall stretching (uniform cell 0.5 E rho*/rho_s; doubled ribbon walls 0.45), a linear shear profile over half the core depth, and a 16 mm transfer length, about 1.7 cells. Homogenisation is marginal there and cell-scale peaks are not modelled. The W direction governs over L on both strengths.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A cell-resolved finite-element model of a free core edge, or the panel test above.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: The cure leaves the faces in compression balanced by core tension. This card takes it as not driving global buckling or crimping, because the wall's net membrane force is unchanged (this seat's argument). It adds it in full to yield, wrinkling, dimpling and the scarf; for wrinkling that is conservative, since the core's tension near the face resists the wrinkle.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A sandwich-shell buckling analysis with the layer-wise residual state.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: 028b's fixed 30:1 scarf binds at its projected 10 MPa screen, so the cure compression costs usage (0.972 to 1.052); 028's sizing rule restores it at 30.44:1 for 0.16 kg. retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A measured Be scarf allowable and the splice-at-scarf detail.

This card notes the lever and does not take it.

retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: Splice-fill properties and a splice coupon in in-plane tension.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: 037's shear-lag screen holds each face at the core's expansion (0.227 after the 250 F cure). That needs the core to carry 47 times the in-plane force at which its walls yield. CR-1457, Hexcel AGU 075b and NASA TM-4585 treat the core's in-plane stiffness and thermal force as negligible; on that premise the continuous core carries no mismatch shear and a free core edge reads 1.17 / 0.83.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A curved Be/CR-III panel cured with AF 163-2U, cycled over 271-302 K, strain-gauged at a core splice, at a face scarf and in the field, then sectioned.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: The free-edge shear uses this seat's homogenised model: K_biax from wall stretching (uniform cell 0.5 E rho*/rho_s; doubled ribbon walls 0.45), a linear shear profile over half the core depth, and a 16 mm transfer length, about 1.7 cells. Homogenisation is marginal there and cell-scale peaks are not modelled. The W direction governs over L on both strengths.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A cell-resolved finite-element model of a free core edge, or the panel test above.

retained_037b_owner_rows.claim: The cure leaves the faces in compression balanced by core tension. This card takes it as not driving global buckling or crimping, because the wall's net membrane force is unchanged (this seat's argument). It adds it in full to yield, wrinkling, dimpling and the scarf; for wrinkling that is conservative, since the core's tension near the face resists the wrinkle.
retained_037b_owner_rows.needed_to_ground: A sandwich-shell buckling analysis with the layer-wise residual state.

new.title: Test units and calibration description
new.finding: The stored Pach test_depth_m is 1.1 instead of 0.0011. The claimed agreement with the measured 1.1–1.2 mm range is false: the model predicts 1.489–1.541 mm, and it is a peak-depth model compared with a residual dent.
new.proposed_fix: Correct the unit field; report the 24–40% depth overprediction relative to the stated test range and the peak/residual distinction.

new.title: Printed hail masses were replaced unnecessarily
new.finding: IEC Table 3 supplies all six masses. The substituted 35/55/65 mm masses and energies differ from the printed inputs.
new.proposed_fix: Use 20.7/80.2/132.0 g and 7.657344/46.083321/88.894740 J; carry the recomputed all-energy dents. The 50.8 mm design case is unchanged.

new.title: 55 mm growth entry
new.finding: The clamped 55 mm threshold is 19.176311 mm, not deeper than the 23.237218 mm core.
new.proposed_fix: Correct the table cell; keep its model and boundary qualifications.

new.title: Perry factor does not follow the cited equation
new.finding: The filed 4.095817936 differs from 3.454499160 obtained from the stated L/1000 bow, direct magnified bending and an independent quadratic root. The pinned 022d table also gives 3.454499160.
new.proposed_fix: Replace the non-governing factor and add the direct-stress check. The overall nominal 1.258252477 is unchanged.

new.title: Repeated-strike probability and approximation
new.finding: The stored count is ln(2)/Pf. For independent equal-risk trials the exact real-valued 50% count is ln(2)/[-ln(1-Pf)]. The design case changes 61.224523/13.134564 to 60.877292/12.784859. Repeated identical loading of the same Weibull specimen is not automatically an independent trial.
new.proposed_fix: Label the rare-event approximation and provide exact counts and integer ceilings: the 25 mm sectored-flexure lower bound is 485, not 484. Define strike location/damage history before treating counts as storm reliability.

new.title: Additional feasible P3 witnesses
new.finding: The published priced witnesses reproduce, but a separate multistart search finds better points. Walls 1.5/2.0/3.0 mm yield SF 0.805476/0.483053/0.223304 versus 0.800189/0.469060/null. At 303.532 MPa film allowable, SF 0.975445 uses 848.604 kg film, versus 0.975205 and 880.534 kg.
new.proposed_fix: Retain filed points as local witnesses, add the independently verified alternatives and distinguish an unsuccessful search from an infeasibility proof. None of these wall/tear cases reaches SF 1.

new.title: Usage above one marked feasible
new.finding: Two patch-price rows and all four denser-core rows have feasible=true although their optimism usage exceeds one; 028b explicitly excludes that interpretation.
new.proposed_fix: Set design-feasible=false or rename the flag to geometry_solved, preserving the numeric usage.

new.title: First half-kilogram times are sampled too late
new.finding: Twenty-four stored event-time fields differ outside tolerance. A 100 mm hole reaches 0.5 kg at 0.464206 s, not 0.770164 s; the torn bay reaches it at 0.000837478 s, not 0.001535376 s.
new.proposed_fix: Root mass(t)-0.5 using dense output or an event function. Main touchdown and flow conclusions reproduce.

new.title: Summary excludes small tools and the 8 lb bird
new.finding: The stated lambda range 0.077–0.258 omits the small-tool 0.061648 and 8 lb bird 0.314510. Both still lie below the adopted 0.630970 map cutoff.
new.proposed_fix: State threat-specific ranges and retain the distinction between crushed diameter and dent depth.

new.title: Contour interval is not detection performance
new.finding: The primary Prior thesis uses 0.2 mm contours as a dent-diameter measurement threshold. It does not establish 0.2 mm detection resolution or reliable identification of critical damage. Tap-test values are disbond PoD on aluminium.
new.proposed_fix: Report the measurement definition and retain unknown Be/SiC/PBO detection capability.

new.title: Four selected removals do not bound all damage cases
new.finding: All 56 reported frame comparisons reproduce with radial loads based on planar triangle areas. Across six f4 and nine f5 edge classes the stress ratio spans 1.959485–3.270739 and peak tension 0–1019.372 MPa. A static rigid-joint calculation does not prove a dynamic cascade after every possible member loss.
new.proposed_fix: Pin mesh, pressure quadrature, joint model and removed edges; distinguish selected cases from an envelope. Keep nonlinear and installed-joint verification open.

new.title: Projected fracture screen stated as a certainty
new.finding: The slit lengths and 0.838835 merged-bay SF reproduce, but substitute-polymer toughness and assumed effective modulus do not demonstrate that every puncture opens an installed PBO bay.
new.proposed_fix: Use conditional fracture-screen language. Installed orthotropic film toughness, notch response, prestress and arrest features remain unknown.

new.title: Ground contact, inventory and heaviness conventions
new.finding: The trajectory assumes a neutral full sphere at 500 m with non-air mass 4889.444 kg, rather than proving the built 028b/022d inventory. Centre altitude zero is also ten metres below first contact for an R10 sphere. About 5131 kg is incoming gas, not the net buoyancy deficit.
new.proposed_fix: Specify carried inventory, sagged displacement and initial restraint; stop at centre height 10 m above terrain. For the same gross reference, torn-bay first-contact speeds remain 23.099647–34.541863 m/s and net heaviness about 4889 kg.

new.title: Venting is a conditional load reduction, not a qualified operation
new.finding: The 0.458903732 pressure fraction and 2645.660029 kg use the 500 m full-volume state. At sea-level ISA the same absolute differential requires 2912.791114 kg on that convention. Venting an airborne neutral hull makes it descend; it needs a supported landing/handling sequence. Regulatory speeds are analogous test criteria, not established safe hull speeds.
new.proposed_fix: Retain the arithmetic and require explicit terrain, support, gas volume, atmosphere and valve control. Do not infer a 500 m AGL operating condition solely from a 500 m atmospheric design altitude.

new.title: Unstated modeling choices and material transfers
new.finding: Exact reproduction needs SiC nu=0.16, core E/G scaled linearly with density in pricing, radial/planar nodal loading, a rounded 48.894 kg gas item, and an integral of the expanding hard-impact footprint. The artificial growth law, typical core crush and transferred shell/film properties remain unvalidated.
new.proposed_fix: Pin these input conventions and their PROJECTION tags. Keep primary measured properties distinct from transferred allowables and from predictions of installed damage tolerance.

inherited.claim: The dent-growth criterion is this seat's derivation: the face's fixed membrane force pR/4 on a paraboloid dent's curvature, against the core's crush strength less its share of the pressure, with the patch's plate buckling force taken off. No opened page prints it. Castanie, the CAI literature on face wrinkling over crushed core, and McGowan and Ambur's preload threshold support the mechanism, not the numbers.

inherited.claim: The lost-core patch is read clamped (54.8 mm) and simply supported (27.1 mm); the real edge, a face continuous over intact core, lies between. The pressure that holds the face on the crushed core is a barrier this static reading ignores.
inherited.needed_to_ground: A plate-on-crushable-foundation analysis of the dented patch, or the coupon test above.

inherited.claim: The dent model (face membrane plus core crush over a plastic spread) is this seat's. It reads Pach's test within its 1.1-1.2 mm and 30 mm, and Clarke's FE at about half the FE depth. Hail is read three ways (fluid, Shi-calibrated, all energy) that span ten times in depth.
inherited.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a beryllium-faced CR-III panel at 25-75 mm and IEC velocities.

inherited.claim: No impact, puncture or through-thickness ductility data exist for thin SR-200 sheet. NASA 1971 calls beryllium's impact resistance extremely low. A cracked outer face vents its core cells; whether the CR-III core is perforated (034's evacuation of every cell) decides whether a crack vents the whole core.
inherited.needed_to_ground: Drop and ice-ball tests on 0.8 mm SR-200 sheet over honeycomb, and the core venting design.

inherited.claim: Each dent is scored alone against gamma 0.564; the as-built imperfection already spends that allowance, so a dent and the as-built shape compete for it.
inherited.needed_to_ground: 015's map with two interacting imperfections, or a measured shell.

inherited.claim: No hail flux (stones per square metre per storm, by size) was sourced, so the number of tube strikes in a storm is not given.
inherited.needed_to_ground: A hail climatology for the site.

inherited.claim: The tube's hail stress uses a shallow-shell-on-foundation reading of a cylinder, a static contact pressure (fluid or Shi-calibrated), no dynamic amplification, and the 14 mm Hexoloy tube data without size scaling. Birds, timber debris and tool drops on the tubes are not scored. No SiC tube impact test was found.
inherited.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a 275 mm, 1.14 mm-wall SiC tube.

inherited.claim: No Zylon/PBO film exists as a sourced product: no modulus, toughness, puncture or tear data. The tear lengths use other films' toughness and a projected modulus. The film is also unprotected from daylight (35 percent strength after six months).
inherited.needed_to_ground: A built 0/90 PBO film with barrier, tested for puncture, slit tear under biaxial load and UV.

inherited.claim: The lost-member screen is linear, rigid-jointed, on f4/f5 geodesics not at 022d's spacing, with lumped pressure loads; joint stiffness is unknown and no nonlinear collapse was run. 026b's discrete model is the place to repeat it.

inherited.needed_to_ground: A membrane analysis of the rhombic bay.

inherited.claim: The descent model is a rigid sphere in ISA with an isothermal fill, a constant drag coefficient 0.2-0.47, added mass 0.5 rho V and no wind; the neutral-buoyancy pressure result assumes the inside air takes the outside temperature.

inherited.claim: At a hole the face reads twice its membrane stress and yields out to 3.9 hole radii; whether the edge crumples and the hole grows while the slow leak keeps the load on is not modelled.
inherited.needed_to_ground: A hole-edge analysis of the sandwich at 300 MPa, or a punctured coupon under biaxial compression.

inherited.claim: No mast contact speed was sourced; TAR 473 and 14 CFR 25.473 stand in, and the 0.5 m contact patch is assumed.
inherited.needed_to_ground: A mooring system design and its contact envelope.

rows.title: Ten-year retention

rows.title: Installed inventory

findings.title: Material and assembly transfers
findings.finding: Inherited Be/core/adhesive strengths, gamma, Q, thin film, scarf average stress, core-cell model and finish transfer do not establish installed hull capability. All 048/040/031 findings are retained.
findings.missing_evidence: Matched material, panel, joint, imperfection and shell tests.

findings.title: Joint weather distributions
findings.finding: MIL marginals do not supply complete coincident T/p/RH. Low-pressure data used are at 1 km, not sea level. Surface and joint hot-humid profiles need declared pressure/lapse assumptions; percentages are not global annual flyability.
findings.missing_evidence: A chosen site/mission joint sounding distribution and design-event definition.

findings.title: Different designs versus one vehicle
findings.finding: Design-family maps reoptimize geometry by weather condition and optimism set. Original ISA hulls fail the inherited pressure screen in some lower-altitude/high-pressure weather. Separate fixed-geometry full-range hulls and their lower lift margins are supplied.
findings.missing_evidence: Choose a build and operating pressure/temperature envelope before an operating claim.

findings.title: Conditional thermal weather scenario
findings.finding: The coupled map shifts inherited clear-sky offsets with air temperature. Cloud, solar, wind, wet optical response, actual dry-sky radiation and thermally coupled buoyancy are not a measured joint weather model.
findings.missing_evidence: Measured optics and local sky/solar/wind histories; coupled thermal validation.

findings.title: Cold interface boundary
findings.finding: About 277 K air is the cold edge of the inherited minimum-W screen in the scanned core range. A 0.05 K interval separates optimistic exclusion from first fully feasible tabulation. Source strength transfer and restraint dominate this numerical precision.
findings.missing_evidence: Cold assembled-interface tests and validated spatial restraint.

findings.title: Dew/frost rate and retention
findings.finding: Large-sphere convection, Lewis analogy, grey sky, constant capacities, nucleation, droplet pinning, emissivity under wetting and the cold frost scenario are unmeasured. All deposition is retained. Constant-climate dry-start results do not predict a wet-start transient.
findings.missing_evidence: Coating coupons and large-curvature wetting/thermal night measurements.

findings.title: Exterior water and rewetting
findings.finding: The 0.1 kg/m² exterior term is an allowance, not a measured retained film. Extra preexisting-water comparisons are arithmetic; no wet-start evaporation or drainage was solved. Interior absorption may recover after baking.
findings.missing_evidence: Drainage, water uptake, seal moisture and repeated-night exposure tests.

findings.title: Water-control installed costs
findings.finding: Drainage retention, low-emittance switching, cover hardware, heaters, cables and power-system installation are unpriced. Battery conversion uses the inherited 108 usable Wh/kg planning assumption; no mass-free mitigation is credited.
findings.missing_evidence: An installed bill and wet-environment performance for the selected mitigation.

findings.title: Gas service assumptions
findings.finding: Leakage, scarf permeability, 90% conditioning and connected core pores are projected. The 24h pressure/inventory calculation is a conditional bound on sampled geometries, not a sealed-life result or a measured temperature law.
findings.missing_evidence: Whole-hull leaks, pore venting, desorption and permeability versus temperature.

findings.title: Retained mechanical weather conventions
findings.finding: Wind load, pad sizing and reference convection retain 048 reference-density conventions. Mean centre pressure omits a full finite-height hydrostatic shell load. Fatigue, local support details, control and propulsion remain outside the payload screen.
findings.missing_evidence: Weather-dependent installed loads, local support design and controlled-flight analysis.

findings.title: Near-boundary numerical interpretation
findings.finding: Tables are projections with interpolation and scanned geometry bounds. Reported 0.1 K limits should not be interpreted as operational tolerances or probabilistic accuracy. Numerical checks do not validate the inherited material models.
findings.missing_evidence: Independent card check and higher-fidelity model validation.

findings.title: Saturation formula annotation
findings.finding: The es_water docstring names 1981; coefficients are the Buck 1996 update verified against NCAR. The code was preserved after pinning in the retry request. There is no numerical change.
findings.missing_evidence: Use the corrected source annotation in METHOD and SOURCE-AUDIT.

findings.title: Radius scope of hot-day failure
findings.finding: No sampled radius 10/12/15/20/30 m floats on the declared 10% hot profile, even with all four endpoints. This does not prove impossibility at every radius or under every pressure/profile assumption.
findings.missing_evidence: A separately defined expanded-size or revised-design study if required.

inherited_037b.claim: 037's shear-lag screen holds each face at the core's expansion (0.227 after the 250 F cure). That needs the core to carry 47 times the in-plane force at which its walls yield. CR-1457, Hexcel AGU 075b and NASA TM-4585 treat the core's in-plane stiffness and thermal force as negligible; on that premise the continuous core carries no mismatch shear and a free core edge reads 1.17 / 0.83.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A curved Be/CR-III panel cured with AF 163-2U, cycled over 271-302 K, strain-gauged at a core splice, at a face scarf and in the field, then sectioned.

inherited_037b.claim: The free-edge shear uses this seat's homogenised model: K_biax from wall stretching (uniform cell 0.5 E rho*/rho_s; doubled ribbon walls 0.45), a linear shear profile over half the core depth, and a 16 mm transfer length, about 1.7 cells. Homogenisation is marginal there and cell-scale peaks are not modelled. The W direction governs over L on both strengths.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A cell-resolved finite-element model of a free core edge, or the panel test above.

inherited_037b.claim: The cure leaves the faces in compression balanced by core tension. This card takes it as not driving global buckling or crimping, because the wall's net membrane force is unchanged (this seat's argument). It adds it in full to yield, wrinkling, dimpling and the scarf; for wrinkling that is conservative, since the core's tension near the face resists the wrinkle.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A sandwich-shell buckling analysis with the layer-wise residual state.

inherited_037b.claim: 028b's fixed 30:1 scarf binds at its projected 10 MPa screen, so the cure compression costs usage (0.972 to 1.052); 028's sizing rule restores it at 30.44:1 for 0.16 kg. The 10 MPa screen is not a measured Be scarf allowable, and a filled core splice at the scarf may change the local face stress.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A measured Be scarf allowable and the splice-at-scarf detail.

inherited_037b.claim: 028b's faces are pinned by its fixed 30:1 scarf. Without any cure compression a 30.44:1 scarf would let them thin, to usage 0.894. 028b gives no reason for fixing 30:1, such as machining, overlap, peel or panel-edge limits. This card notes the lever and does not take it.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: 028b's owner states why the scarf is fixed at 30:1, or re-runs the least set with the scarf ratio free.

inherited_037b.claim: Whether 028's filled 0.5 mm core splice carries the core's in-plane force (no free edge) is not shown; the fill's modulus and its bond to the cut cell walls are unsourced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Splice-fill properties and a splice coupon in in-plane tension.

inherited_037b.claim: The residual is a sustained shear on the core. On the minimum-average W strength (25 psi) it reads 0.83 at a free edge after the 250 F cure. Honeycomb creep and day-night fatigue under sustained shear are not sourced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Sustained-load and cyclic shear data for CR-III 5056 3/8-1.0.

inherited_037b.claim: The cure-or-Tg rule (108-121 C for AF 163-2U) is sourced qualitatively; no measured stress-free temperature or relaxed fraction for AF 163 was found.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A bimaterial-strip or panel-curvature measurement with the actual cure cycle.

inherited_037b.claim: Room-temperature pastes (EA 9394 class) carry no sourced honeycomb bond data, fillet mass or flatwise strength; they are priced at AF's areal weight.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Honeycomb flatwise and climbing-drum data for a room-temperature system at a weighed areal mass.

inherited_037b.claim: Hexcel prints only thickness-direction expansion for glass and aramid cores; their in-plane values are proxies here. The carbon core UCF-145 (12.8 kg/m3, second-hand shear data, W strength 97 kPa) has no sourced in-plane expansion or compressive modulus and is not priced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: In-plane expansion and compressive data for candidate non-metallic cores.

inherited_037b.claim: NASA/SDSU co-cured-panel studies report the face/core cure mismatch as cell-wall distortion and face waviness. That is a source of the wrinkle coefficient's waviness (MAINLINE-032), not of bond shear.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Measured face waviness after an AF 163-2U cure on CR-III.

inherited_037b.claim: 5056-H39 foil properties were not sourced: the wall stiffness uses 5056-H14 bulk (67 GPa, 2700 kg/m3) and the wall allowable the measured 5052-H39 foil yield (227.5 MPa).
Inserts, closeouts and 037's mooring pads constrain the mismatch locally; they are not scored here.

rows.issue: No site elevation, terrain, minimum hull clearance, altitude ceiling or required 500m condition has been authorised. Centre 10m is ground tangency at sea level; 100m is only an illustrative 90m clearance.
rows.next_evidence: Specify centre-height range relative to surveyed terrain, weather set, clearance and whether 500m means ISA free float or a minimum on every design day.

rows.issue: 019 specifies conditions at one altitude, not a vertical profile. A 6.5K/km lapse and constant e/p were imposed. At the 100m floor, isothermal optimistic climate mass is 11.73kg versus 55.34kg with the chosen lapse; both-weather values are 403.66 versus 441.77kg.
rows.next_evidence: Supply measured or approved temperature, pressure, humidity and inversion profiles, including joint extremes and occurrence probabilities.

rows.issue: The conservative high-pressure humid day becomes supersaturated in the all-weather 500m-floor diagnostic. The 0/10/100m-floor main cases are unsaturated in the stated model. Continuing an unsaturated lapse through cloud is not a physical forecast.
rows.next_evidence: Use a moist atmospheric profile with cloud/condensate treatment; do not treat that diagnostic height as an operational guarantee.

rows.issue: A fixed evacuated hull has one passive equilibrium per weather profile and carried load. Positive C raises its ISA float altitude; C=0 cannot float at 500m ISA and satisfy the illustrative sea-level-ground clearance on both 019 hot-day extremes. Static equilibrium does not provide station keeping.
rows.next_evidence: Resolve the mission requirement; size active altitude control, tethering, launch, landing, descent-rate and gust response if needed.

rows.issue: Climate is absent mass; water, contamination and gas are carried mass. 021 rev1 has a 5% placeholder, no separate climate rows or explicit seam budget. Recasting that placeholder is a new budget assumption.
rows.next_evidence: Approve one common itemised gross mass ledger, including payload status, before treating cross-card points as the same vehicle.

rows.issue: SR-200 345MPa is a tensile minimum transferred to compression. The 379.2MPa endpoint is a historical lot result; continuous interpolated strength is not a procureable design allowable. 021 rev1 inherits 283MPa at E290GPa.
rows.next_evidence: Obtain gauge-, direction-, lot-, temperature- and post-form compression and modulus allowables.

rows.issue: The least-set P2 points need multi-metre square-equivalent panels at roughly 0.65–0.72mm face gauge. The nominal today 0.9144m seam-equivalent stock size is itself not established at those gauges.
rows.next_evidence: Supplier-confirm formed sheet sizes, gauges, thickness distribution, yield and joining geometry.

rows.issue: The hemisphere-derived 0.2/1 branch rule and 018 interpolation to 0.2+0.4min(Vc,2) have not been validated for the complete sphere. Numerical least-set membership is conditional on these bounds.
rows.next_evidence: Correlate full-shell imperfection-sensitive nonlinear analysis and representative structural testing.

rows.issue: Wrinkle coefficients between 0.33 and 0.82 and published typical core properties are used for a curved sandwich. The catalogue includes transferred moduli and scaled cores; the winner is the sourced light 5056 core, but no assembly allowable exists.
rows.next_evidence: Test curvature, cell depth, orthotropy, face/core bond and biaxial wrinkling/crimp/crush/dimpling at service temperature.

rows.issue: P2 seams and bond films are a mass recipe, not checked structural joints. P3 percent joints are an allowance, not strength or rotational stiffness. Folded source joints sized at p0 cannot automatically take a larger float pressure.
rows.next_evidence: Size and qualify seal, splice, node and load-introduction details at the maximum service pressure, including stiffness, eccentricity, fatigue and leakage.

rows.issue: The passing P3 keeps a 3900MPa SiC tube compression value, 410GPa modulus, 1.5GPa/970kg/m3 film and metre-scale thin curved tubes. These are not a demonstrated assembly or a safe tensile/bending allowable.
rows.next_evidence: Carry tube-scale brittle reliability, post-form flaw statistics, film biaxial/creep/UV/seam/barrier properties and manufacture into the model.

rows.issue: FIX-A triangular load sharing is used. FIX-B SP-8007 axial-cylinder knockdown is transferred to curved ceramic members; Perry and k=0.2 global continuum equations remain inherited idealisations.
rows.next_evidence: Validate curved member local buckling, imperfections, ceramic tension/compression interaction and discrete-frame modes with actual node stiffness.

rows.issue: 022b's s/(16R) displacement loss is applied as reduced volume at every altitude. Film shape may change with pressure, and the spherical arc/member model is approximate for 6m bays on R10m.
rows.next_evidence: Solve coupled membrane shape, true enclosed volume, pressure and frame load path; verify the global continuum approximation and spacing bounds.

rows.issue: Mode scores use uniform centre pressure, no internal-pressure relief and fixed material properties. Local bottom pressure is about a further 0.1% higher, while gradients, thermal mismatch, wind, attached loads and descent transients are unscored.
rows.next_evidence: Set structural design factors and loads independently of the SF=1 screening threshold; include nonuniform pressure and thermal/wind/handling loads.

rows.issue: The calculation retains optimistic 019 nonclimate loads and the full 100kg system floor even on conservative weather. This isolates weather; it does not qualify the conservative pump/battery/rain/contamination hardware package.
rows.next_evidence: Qualify 24h sealed service and internal gas inventory, or recalculate with measured leakage, pumping, rain/ice retention and all installed systems.
